POWER RANKINGS

Twelve teams. One very opinionated list. The weekly pecking order, straight from the Commish.

Movement since after week 3.

+1 Moved up-1 Moved down— Even No change

  1. 01

    DonkeyWoodDean

    — Even

    Until Brett gives me a reason to move him, his ass is staying right here. Mels-16 is making a hell of a case for number one, but undefeated buys you the benefit of the doubt. Gibbs, Olave, and company keep finding ways to make me look stupid for picking against them. You have the crown, Brett. Please try to enjoy it without making the rest of us regret having ears.

  2. 02

    Mels-16

    — Even

    Laid the smack down on the Commish and remains firmly in the top two. I scored 165.42 and still lost by 31.20, which feels like something I should be able to report to the fucking police. McMillan went nuts, Kyren went nuts, Bijan went nuts. Apparently drafting half the first four rounds continues to work. You are knocking on Brett’s door, Mark. Another week like that and I might have to let you in.

  3. 03

    Mark’s Team

    +1

    The receivers are pretty meh outside of JJ, but Bowers and that running back room give this team a damn solid foundation. McCaffrey is still McCaffrey, and Bowers can make up for a lot of bullshit elsewhere. The problem is that when Jefferson and DeVonta are out, the replacement receivers do not exactly make me fear for my life. Third is a vote for the talent when this squad is healthy. Please keep enough of it on the field to justify me putting you here.

  4. 04

    Silence of the Lamb

    +1

    Call me a homer all you want. I am 1–3 with the third-most points, and I am not ranking this team like it forgot how to play football because the schedule keeps taking a shit on my chest. Lamb and Javonte just combined for 75.60, and somehow that bought me another loss. Is fourth generous? Maybe. Am I the one holding the pen? Absolutely. File your complaints directly into the trash. I WILL NEVER FUCKING STOP!

  5. 05

    Dillon’s Team

    +3

    On paper, this team looks really damn solid. Cook, Judkins, and Chase Brown give you a running back room I actually like, and if Chase starts turning more of those carries into points, this gets scary in a hurry. Higgins just reminded everyone he can still ruin an opponent’s afternoon. I need the receivers to stay healthy, though, because those Q tags are starting to look like decorations. Up three spots. Please do not make me apologize for liking this team a second time.

  6. 06

    Chris’s Team

    — Even

    There are a lot of question marks here, and most of them are attached to somebody’s body. At full strength, Chase, Rice, Watson, and company can absolutely compete. At whatever the hell strength last week was, you scored 61.58 and left Monangai’s 31 on the bench. I still like the ceiling enough to keep you sixth, but the healthy version of this team needs to start showing up. You are getting the last seat before the talent gap. Do not confuse that with me being comfortable.

    GAP IN TALENT

  7. 07

    Beast Infection

    +2

    Nico Collins. DOG. Kenneth Walker. DOG. Everyone else? A whole lot of meh. Those two just combined for 67.70, which is a pretty effective way to drag the rest of the roster to a win. Stevenson can help, but I still need somebody else to give me a reason to get excited. You are up two spots because the top dogs are doing top-dog shit. Let’s get them some help before we start planning a parade.

  8. 08

    Daniel’s Primo Team

    +2

    Puka is obviously great, Michael Wilson has been a diamond in the rough, and McBride is the number-one tight end in football in my book. That is a pretty nice starting point for a team I have spent three weeks calling shit. Maye’s 27.16 last week is exactly the kind of thing that makes me reconsider how much shit I want to talk. Keep that going and squeeze more production out of the running backs, and we might actually have a contender. The rest of the roster still makes me nervous, but eighth comes with considerably less disgust than tenth did.

  9. 09

    Slim Pickens

    -6

    The biggest drop in my rankings yet. Third to ninth, and I still do not know what the fuck is going on because I love this team. Taylor, Adams, Pickens, and that depth should not have me writing this paragraph. I picked you to knock off Brett, and you thanked me by losing by 65. Apparently compliments are not working, so we are trying public humiliation. Consider ninth a motivational speech with considerably more swearing. Light a fire under this squad before I have to find another floor.

    LARGE GAP IN TALENT

  10. 10

    Gotham Knights

    -3

    I do not know what to say anymore. JSN is on the squad, so I guess that is good, but the surrounding talent is not giving him much to work with. Starting McLaurin for zero last week did not exactly help the situation either. It might be time to see what JSN could bring back in depth, because one dude cannot be the entire fucking Batmobile. Down three spots. The Bat-Signal is on, but right now it is mostly a distress call.

  11. 11

    Overdue Bills

    +1

    You are not moving up because I suddenly fell in love with this team. You are moving up because West Coast got worse. Hubbard and Doubs deserve credit for last week, but one good afternoon does not erase everything I have said about this roster. I still doubt you win many more games, and the Josh Allen shrine should remain fully operational. Here you go, Mick. Up one spot, back to a normal number, and still absolutely no parade.

  12. 12

    West Coast

    -1

    What the hell happened to Saquon? Achane has disappeared from the starting lineup, Bucky is sliding, and the Jags might have too many mouths to feed for everybody to eat. Nabers has not carried this team out of the basement either, although leaving his 26.20 on the bench last week certainly did not help. If you had told me after the draft that this squad would start 0–4, I would have laughed and assumed you benched everyone to give the league a chance. Turns out you did not need to bench everyone. Just enough of the right people.
